evals.prompt: I paused Shantae (Game Boy Color) on the title screen and dumped VRAM (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/vram.bin, 16 KB), OAM (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/oam.bin) and the 12 bytes at $FF40 (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/io.bin), plus a screenshot (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/screenshot.png). Rip the on-screen sprites and both VRAM tile banks to PNGs, in the game's real colors where you can. Tell me what each file is.
evals.expected_output: PNG tile sheets for VRAM bank 0 and bank 1, a sprite sheet in real (inferred) colors, palettes recovered from the screenshot; notes which outputs are grayscale vs real color; notes LCDC sprites-off at frame end.
evals.name: rip-title-graphics
assertions: a PNG contains >=95% of VRAM bank 0's 384 tiles, decoded correctly
a PNG contains >=95% of VRAM bank 1's 384 tiles, decoded correctly
at least one output uses >=5 of the screenshot's real colors (not just grayscale)
Answer says which outputs are grayscale and which are in real color
Answer flags that LCDC=0xE5 has sprites off although sprites are on screen
Text read from the graphics is accurate
Advice is feasible with BizHawk (doesn't tell the user to read CGB palette RAM via $FF68/$FF69 writes, which BizHawk ignores)

evals.prompt: Using these Shantae title-screen dumps (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/vram.bin, <workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/oam.bin, <workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/io.bin) and screenshot (<workspace>/inputs/shantae_title/screenshot.png), check whether decoding the video state actually reproduces the screenshot exactly. Give me the pixel match percentage, and if it isn't 100%, figure out why and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Initial match ~94.56% because LCDC=0xE5 has sprites disabled at frame end while the Press Start plate is sprites; with LCDC overridden to 0xE7 the match is 100.00%.
evals.name: verify-title-decode
assertions: a rendered 160x144 screen in outputs is pixel-identical to the screenshot
Reports the as-dumped match (~94.56%)
Identifies LCDC bit 1 (sprites off at frame end) as the cause
Is honest that colors came from the screenshot, so 100% checks structure, not RGB
Advice is feasible with BizHawk (doesn't tell the user to read CGB palette RAM via $FF68/$FF69 writes, which BizHawk ignores)

evals.prompt: Get the Game Boy Color palettes from this capture and confirm your decode matches the screenshot: <workspace>/inputs/shantae_black/vram.bin, <workspace>/inputs/shantae_black/oam.bin, <workspace>/inputs/shantae_black/io.bin, <workspace>/inputs/shantae_black/screenshot.png. It's from Shantae, early after boot.
evals.expected_output: Notices the screenshot is a uniform black frame (a transition), so recovered palettes are meaningless (only black) and a 100% match proves nothing; recommends capturing a frame with visible content.
evals.name: black-frame-trap
assertions: (fact) the screenshot is a single uniform color
Says the screenshot is entirely black
Says the 100% match proves nothing / can't confirm the decode
Doesn't present the all-black palettes as the game's real palettes
Recommends recapturing a frame with visible content (after the fade)
Advice is feasible with BizHawk (doesn't tell the user to read CGB palette RAM via $FF68/$FF69 writes, which BizHawk ignores)
Text read from the graphics is accurate

evals.prompt: <workspace>/inputs/nes_chr/chr.bin is 8 KB of NES pattern-table (CHR) data I pulled from a game. Render all of it as a tile sheet PNG, 16 tiles wide, and tell me the image dimensions.
evals.expected_output: A 128x256 PNG of 512 tiles decoded with NES planar 2bpp (8 bytes plane 0, then 8 bytes plane 1, bit 7 leftmost).
evals.name: nes-chr-sheet
assertions: sheet.png is 128x256 (16 tiles wide, 512 tiles)
every tile matches an independent NES planar decode, in order
sheet is not decoded with the Game Boy (interleaved) layout by mistake
Answer states 128x256

notes: <workspace> is skills/tile-graphics-workspace/ (gitignored). The Shantae inputs are dumps of a commercial ROM, so they are not committed: recreate them with bizhawk_dump_memory (VRAM, OAM, System Bus $FF40 length 12) and bizhawk_screenshot at the frames described in research/06-tile-graphics-skill-eval.md. inputs/nes_chr/chr.bin is synthetic and generated as described there.
